Title: A legal opening can permanently stall the economy
Observation: Three Markets cost 75 Cycles; one DNS link spends the last 5. After Save → Continue, there are no producers, inputs, affordable replacements, or undo records. A 100-second probe remained at zero resources.
Action: Guarantee an emergency Cycles/reconnection path or sufficient salvage.
Acceptance: Recover the legal zero-resource opening after fresh Continue through guaranteed salvage or emergency supply; keep every reachable run recoverable.

Title: Infrastructure bypasses ICE affordability and can mint Tools
Observation: A Market placed in ICE with zero Tools succeeds and takes the balance to −1. After the tick clamps it to zero, undo refunds an unpaid Tool.
Action: Validate the complete cost, including ICE, before placement; refund only what was paid.
Acceptance: At zero Tools an ICE placement is refused with no charge or node; undo never refunds more than the verified payment.

Title: Advertised tunnel capacity is not a throughput ceiling
Observation: The congestion floor leaves 10% of arbitrarily large input. A DNS fixture reported capacity 3/s, offered 115.4/s, and modeled delivery 11.54/s.
Action: Clarify whether capacity is a hard ceiling or an intentionally soft threshold; then align admission behavior, balance and telemetry.
Acceptance: Choose hard or soft capacity explicitly; offered 115.4/s on a rated 3/s edge obeys the chosen admission rule and matching telemetry.

Title: Converter requests and outputs do not count toward load
Observation: A Market debited 3 Intel and emitted 3 input packets while its edge reported offered load 0/s. Shared trunks omit processor traffic too.
Action: Include input and return traffic in the capacity model.
Acceptance: Account for processor input and output on all traversed edges; three input requests cannot report zero offered load.

Title: Disabled junctions forward for free
Observation: An OFF Market and its child remain reachable and the OFF edge still has telemetry. Its outgoing forwarding incurs no upkeep or noise; the fixture charges only the enabled child's link.
Action: Define production-off versus network-off explicitly and charge forwarding consistently.
Acceptance: Define production-off versus routing-off; forwarded traffic pays its intended upkeep and noise even when local production is disabled.

Title: Disabled Markets still sell passing Intel
Observation: Intel passing through an OFF Market still becomes Cash. A prepaid inbound request also completes after shutdown; define whether that existing work should finish, buffer or cancel separately from pass-through selling.
Action: Require an operational Market before conversion.
Acceptance: An OFF or otherwise non-operational Market cannot silently convert passing Intel; any permitted draining behavior is explicit.

Title: Rebuilt links leave packets on obsolete routes
Observation: A packet stores node IDs for A→B→C2. Reconnect A to D before arrival: its first edge now uses new geometry, but its stored next hop still references B.
Action: Version edges and invalidate replaced-edge traffic, or repath at junction arrivals.
Acceptance: Reparent A from B to D while a packet is in flight; it follows a valid live route or is cancelled under a stated policy.

Title: Advanced Cycles producers reject residential Cycles ground
Observation: The GDD says Package and Cryptojacker can use any Cycles ground, while placement excludes The Sprawl because residential is absent from ZONE_RES. The restriction may be intentional; the communicated rule is inconsistent.
Action: Reconcile the intended district rule and its descriptions, using one authoritative mapping.
Acceptance: Choose whether residential is valid advanced Cycles ground; all previews, tool help and design documentation use that same mapping.

Title: Construction can obstruct an existing tunnel
Observation: A footprint may include road cells if at least half its cells belong to a building. Placement checks other structures, but not existing tunnel cells.
Action: Reject conflicting footprints or preview and reroute affected links.
Acceptance: Reject a footprint over a tunnel or commit a reviewed reroute; no completed construction leaves traffic intersecting blocked geometry.

Title: Rendered buildings and simulated occupancy disagree
Observation: At city seed 12345, a tile/block comparison finds 15 vacancy disagreements near slums boundaries and 53 Farm blocks whose narrow rendered footprint disagrees with wider collision. One authoritative geometry fix covers both.
Action: Generate one authoritative block descriptor for rendering, placement, coverage, and routing.
Acceptance: Rendering, placement, coverage and road routing consume one authoritative building geometry; verify slums boundaries and narrowed Farm blocks.

Title: Undo can leave a nonexistent pending tunnel source
Observation: Place a producer, arm a tunnel from it, then undo its placement. pending_child still references the erased node; the next preview accesses invalid routing state.
Action: Clear pending references and route caches when their node disappears.
Acceptance: Undo the armed source's placement; pending references and preview caches clear without invalid node access.

Title: Undo can leave an invalid selected tunnel
Observation: Select a newly built tunnel and undo construction. Its node survives with tunnel type '', but the inspector still looks up TUNNEL_DEFS using that empty key.
Action: Clear edge selection when its edge is removed; validate before inspection.
Acceptance: Undo a selected edge; selection clears or moves to a valid node and the inspector never indexes an empty tunnel definition.

Title: Cutting or rerouting a swept link does not break the trace
Observation: Cutting the targeted tunnel still causes a four-second blackout and 25-Cash penalty. Traversal follows stored node IDs without validating live adjacency. The advertised 'go quiet' action affects future charge, not active traversal.
Action: Validate the traced connection at every step and cancel or repath it.
Acceptance: Sever and reparent an actively swept edge; sweep traversal validates live adjacency and countermeasure help states what quieting can actually do.

Title: The advance warning already quarantines the target
Observation: During the six-second warning, the target's quarantine is continuously refreshed. The attack has already impaired the network while the banner says impact is still ahead.
Action: Apply quarantine on arrival, or label the opening phase as an immediate lockdown.
Acceptance: During the advertised warning period, no quarantine applies before impact unless the warning explicitly labels an immediate lockdown.

Title: 'Run linked structures' accepts disabled operations
Observation: The contract counts connected non-Proxy nodes without checking their enabled state. OFF infrastructure can satisfy an active-operation objective.
Action: Define eligible operating structures and require them to be enabled.
Acceptance: OFF nodes cannot satisfy an objective phrased as running linked operations; define and display its exact eligibility policy.

Title: Reload inflates fractional Cash packets
Observation: Saving an in-flight packet valued at 0.5 and loading it restores value 1.0. The value field is omitted, then defaults to one on delivery.
Action: Serialize and restore packet value.
Acceptance: A fractional 0.5-Cash packet retains 0.5 after Save, in-place Load and fresh Continue and banks exactly once.

Title: Continuing erases the threat subsystem
Observation: Saves omit sweeps, sweep charge, Notoriety, blackout and quarantine timers. A fresh Continue resets them; in-place loading can instead retain unrelated current state.
Action: Persist the complete threat subsystem and restore it as one transaction.
Acceptance: Sweep route, phase, charge, Notoriety, blackout and quarantine resume identically in fresh and in-place load.

Title: Continuing removes a paid Overclock
Observation: The payment is saved, but boost_t is not. Saving during the 20-second boost loses the remaining benefit on Continue.
Action: Persist the remaining boost duration.
Acceptance: A paid boost resumes with its saved remaining duration; payment and benefit cannot diverge across reload.

Title: Continuing discards accepted and completed contracts
Observation: The save contains no board, deadlines, completed rewards, next contract ID, or generation cooldown. Accepted work and unclaimed rewards disappear.
Action: Persist the contract lifecycle and its generation state.
Acceptance: Offers, acceptance, completion, unclaimed rewards, deadlines and generation state survive fresh and in-place load without duplicate rewards.

Title: Continuing resets cumulative run statistics
Observation: The saved time is the animation clock. Active-play duration, delivered packets, peak Trace and peak Cash rate are absent, so a resumed run's result excludes earlier activity.
Action: Persist cumulative metrics and a captured victory result.
Acceptance: Run duration, delivered count, peak metrics and captured victory result preserve their accumulated values after Continue.

Title: Load accepts invalid game schemas
Observation: A JSON object such as {} passes the top-level check, installs an empty node set, and returns success. Simulation then accesses a nonexistent Hub; node types and packet indices are also unchecked.
Action: Validate version, resources, node graph and packet fields in temporary state before replacing the session.
Acceptance: Reject empty, malformed or unsupported save schemas before touching the active run; validate hub, graph, routes and numeric ranges.

Title: The only save is truncated before replacement is secure
Observation: Opening the save in WRITE mode destroys the previous contents before the new write completes. An interrupted write can lose the usable save; final write errors are not checked.
Action: Write a checked temporary file, replace safely, and retain a backup.
Acceptance: An interrupted or failed write preserves the last valid save; return success only after a checked durable write and safe replacement.

Title: Load restarts simulation randomness
Observation: Only the world seed is restored. Regenerating the city restarts the RNG stream instead of restoring packet-loss and contract randomness to the saved point.
Action: Persist simulation RNG state separately from the map seed.
Acceptance: The next simulation random draw after reload equals the uninterrupted run; persist RNG state without losing integer precision.

Title: In-place Load retains undo records from the discarded timeline
Observation: In-place Load retains discarded undo history: the fixture refunds 5 unpaid Cycles, changing 1000 to 1005. It also retains selection, pan and rate/preview state from the other timeline; reset those as one load transaction.
Action: Clear undo and transient action state on load, or restore history belonging to that save.
Acceptance: Loading a prior state clears its discarded undo history and transient selections, drag state, preview and rate sampling; undo cannot mint resources.

Title: Repeatable stockpile rewards bypass the production economy
Observation: The starting 80 Cycles satisfy 20–50-Cycle jobs. A probe claimed 50 Cash and 5 RP while retaining all 80 Cycles; the same stock can qualify again. Stockpile milestones can be intentional, but repeatable payouts undermine the stated supply-chain gate.
Action: Use incremental production or deliveries, or make possession milestones one-time rewards.
Acceptance: Repeatable work cannot pay again for the same unchanged starting stock; define possession rewards as one-time milestones or pay for new deliveries.

Title: Coverage calculation, shape and advertised range disagree
Observation: Production counts a radius-four square while displaying a radius-four circle. Of 225 fixture centers, 164 differ under disk counting. Phishing/Scraper inspector separately advertises six tiles although productive coverage uses four.
Action: Use the same geometry and center for calculation and visualization.
Acceptance: Coverage calculation, displayed shape, center and range text agree; the current square-radius-four and circle/radius-six descriptions cannot coexist.

Title: The sidebar overflows the supported 720-pixel viewport
Observation: At 1280x720, Build status begins at y742 and Tech at y765. Stats also reaches about y750, with status at y756. Reserve a visible feedback region and allow every long tab to scroll.
Action: Allocate remaining height responsively and reserve a visible status region.
Acceptance: Every Build, Tech and Stats action and status remains reachable in the supported 720p viewport at all supported text scales.

Title: The Jobs board has no scrolling
Observation: Three ordinary contract cards extend from y199 to y765; the last action lies below the viewport, without a scroll container.
Action: Make the board scroll within the available sidebar height.
Acceptance: Three or more job cards scroll within the available sidebar; the last claim/accept action remains reachable at 720p.

Title: 200% text size leaves most interface text unchanged
Observation: HUD/body/status stay 18/16/14 pixels and tabs stay 16 pixels. Fixed per-control overrides bypass the scaled theme default.
Action: Scale centralized font tokens and allow layouts to reflow.
Acceptance: At 200% all ordinary HUD, body, status, tab, button and graph text scales under shared tokens and layouts reflow.

Title: Selection prevents tab navigation
Observation: Selecting C2 then choosing Menu leaves the inspector visible and Menu hidden. Arming a tool can likewise retain tunnel selection and suppress Build content; treat navigation and inspection as explicit states.
Action: Decouple navigation state from inspection, or explicitly close inspection when switching tabs.
Acceptance: Switching tabs while inspecting a node or tunnel reveals the chosen tab or explicitly closes the inspector.

Title: Tool help and introductory instructions are hidden
Observation: Armed-tool, hover and C2 Console text are computed inside sel_box, but that parent is visible only when an object is selected.
Action: Show contextual help in a region visible in those states.
Acceptance: Introductory, armed-tool and hover/focus help is visible even with no selected map object.

Title: Action feedback is replaced by generic guidance
Observation: 'Game saved' is replaced by next-step guidance; tool hints can mask failures and rewards. Smokescreen also replaces its sweep-cancel outcome internally before the UI can show it.
Action: Give action results a dedicated timed message channel.
Acceptance: Save success, failed placement, rewards and other action results persist visibly before generic guidance resumes.

Title: Offline alerts omit completely unlinked structures
Observation: Newly placed nodes and children detached by dismantling have parent == −1 and are skipped by the offline alert counter.
Action: Count all intended operations without a live C2 route, with a separate disabled category.
Acceptance: Unlinked new producers and newly detached branches appear in offline diagnostics; intentionally disabled nodes have their own state.

Title: Alert navigation leaves conflicting selections active
Observation: After selecting a tunnel, clicking a Trace or Starved alert selects C2 but retains the tunnel selection. The inspector continues showing the old tunnel; an armed tool can also retain priority.
Action: Clear conflicting selection/tool state before selecting the alert target.
Acceptance: An alert jump establishes one coherent selection and the inspector describes the jumped-to object.

Title: Settings block interaction while the simulation continues
Observation: Opening blocking Settings leaves paused=false. Current processing therefore continues production, contracts and threat clocks. The fresh fixture verifies pause state; it does not claim a full countdown playthrough.
Action: Suspend the simulation while this modal is open and restore the prior pause state.
Acceptance: Opening blocking Settings freezes gameplay while preserving the previous pause state; closing restores that state.

Title: Escape acts behind Settings
Observation: Repeated Escape presses toggle simulation pause/resume while Settings remains visible, instead of dismissing the frontmost screen.
Action: Route Escape to the frontmost modal first.
Acceptance: Escape closes or backs out of the topmost Settings/modal state before changing hidden gameplay pause or tool state.

Title: Gameplay shortcuts pass through blocking modals
Observation: E disables a selected node behind Settings; Delete, undo, overclock and output keys share the unguarded dispatcher. Continuous raw arrow-key polling also pans the camera behind the modal.
Action: Gate gameplay shortcuts by modal context; explicitly allow only intended planning actions.
Acceptance: Blocking modals prevent Delete, output, disable, overclock, undo and map action shortcuts from changing the background run.

Title: Modal keyboard focus remains on background controls
Observation: Focus a build button, open Settings, press Enter: the background build tool activates. The modal neither claims initial focus nor bounds navigation.
Action: Set initial focus, trap it within the modal, and restore it on close.
Acceptance: Opening a modal transfers focus inside and prevents focus or activation of background controls until closing.

Title: The pause menu blocks the advertised mouse planning flow
Observation: The full-screen pause dimmer consumes mouse input, so current pause-to-plan code comments/design intent do not provide usable mouse planning. The review no longer treats this as a demonstrated on-screen promise.
Action: Separate a planning pause from the modal pause menu.
Acceptance: Expose a non-modal planning pause; mouse selection, construction and linking work while simulation remains frozen.

Title: The victory scorecard extends beyond the viewport
Observation: At 1280×720, an unwrapped result label expands the panel to 899 pixels at x460; its right edge reaches x1359.
Action: Wrap result text and center a panel sized against the viewport.
Acceptance: The victory panel wraps and remains wholly within 1280x720, including all supported type scales and a long result string.

Title: Reduced Motion is ignored in the main menu
Observation: With Reduced Motion enabled, menu._process(1) still advances its animation time and drifting packet positions use that time. This is a current state/source check, not a rendered motion-comfort study.
Action: Apply the setting across menu and gameplay animation.
Acceptance: Persisted Reduced Motion gates menu time-driven packet drift and decorative animation as well as gameplay.

Title: Placement validity keeps red/green-only previews
Observation: The footprint preview uses hardcoded green/red even under the colour-blind setting, without a local symbol identifying validity.
Action: Use semantic palette colours plus an OK/blocked symbol and readable reason.
Acceptance: Valid and invalid placement have redundant local symbols/reasons and use semantic palette colors rather than red/green alone.

Title: Decision-critical map colours ignore the colour-blind palette
Observation: Districts and minimap markers use ZONE_COLOR/COLORS, while resource packets use Settings colours. Resource-to-ground matching becomes inconsistent.
Action: Apply one semantic palette to ground, markers and resource cues, reinforced with patterns.
Acceptance: Ground, build chips, map structures, minimap and resource packets use consistent resource semantics when the alternate palette changes.

Title: Palette changes leave cached interface colors stale
Observation: Alternate-palette toggle leaves legend label colors unchanged and unequal to Settings.res_color. GlyphIcon also lacks settings-driven redraw invalidation; the earlier claim that every glyph updates immediately is withdrawn.
Action: Refresh cached UI colour overrides when settings change.
Acceptance: Changing the palette refreshes legend label colors immediately, alongside glyphs and packets.

Title: Slow drags become unintended clicks
Observation: With the viewport pointer explicitly outside the sidebar, twenty movements of 2 pixels total 40 pixels but never set the drag flag. Slow release can therefore place/select or cancel after panning.
Action: Measure total displacement from press and use one shared drag threshold.
Acceptance: Twenty 2-pixel movements after one press count as a drag; release cannot place or cancel after the full 40-pixel displacement.

Title: Middle-mouse panning can remain latched after a UI release
Observation: A Control-consumed middle-button release can leave _panning latched. In the state fixture, subsequent motion with button_mask=0 still moves the camera; the ordinary release path is source-verified.
Action: Capture release globally and reconcile pan state with the actual button state.
Acceptance: A middle-button release over a Control always clears panning; pointer movement afterward cannot move the camera without a held button.

Title: Critical warnings overlap the net-rate text
Observation: Warning rectangle (300,42,359,24) overlaps rate rectangle (312,42,361,22). A separate large-stock stress fixture also pushes the unwrapped resource/goal HUD beyond the right edge; use one responsive HUD layout.
Action: Reserve separate responsive HUD regions for warnings, legend and rates.
Acceptance: Overload or ICE warnings occupy a reserved HUD region separate from economic rates and other text at 720p.

Title: Visible tower rooftops do not match selection targets
Observation: Hit-testing the projected C2 roof-center tile returns no node: the roof is drawn above/right of the ground footprint but _node_at tests ground cells. The fixture derives the projected target and checks it; it is not a rendered mouse-click playtest.
Action: Hit-test the visible silhouette or expose a clear selectable ground marker.
Acceptance: Clicks on the visible tower silhouette select the intended structure, or the selectable ground target is clearly shown and consistently used.

Title: Loading a different seed leaves the previous minimap districts
Observation: The minimap retains its baked texture after seed 42 to 43 regeneration. Load calls that regeneration without invalidating the cache. The fixture checks regeneration and texture retention; the full UI Load click path is source-verified.
Action: Invalidate map-dependent minimap caches after loading.
Acceptance: Loading a different seed rebuilds minimap district texture and state even if node count and camera happen to match.

Title: Converted Proxies retain their original minimap identity
Observation: Rendering uses n.type instead of the relay flag, and the redraw signature tracks node count rather than conversion state.
Action: Use the effective node type and include state revisions in minimap invalidation.
Acceptance: A converted donor appears as a Proxy on the minimap immediately and after loading; effective identity participates in invalidation.

Title: Paused actions can leave the map visually stale
Observation: On a stationary paused view, toggling a selected node changes its enabled state but draw count remains 2. Explicit queue_redraw raises it to 3. Redraw gating checks motion/view/tool activity, not state mutations.
Action: Introduce visual dirty revisions and invalidate on state, selection, settings and final-animation transitions.
Acceptance: Toggle, dismantle, undo and change settings while paused without moving the pointer; the map updates once, then returns to idle redraw behavior.

Title: Culling bounds omit visible routes and selected overlays
Observation: In a constructed orthogonal-detour fixture, a path point is inside the viewport while merged endpoint footprints fail culling; the tunnel and its packets are skipped. A selected-node vision ring can also cross the viewport while its footprint is culled. These are geometric fixtures, not measured natural-route prevalence.
Action: Cache actual path bounds and include visible overlay bounds; retain cheap culling after verifying geometry.
Acceptance: A detour segment and its packets remain visible when endpoints are offscreen; selected coverage/vision rings remain visible wherever they intersect the exposed view.

Title: Restored armed sources permit replacement Undo to lose the old link
Observation: A legal remove-link, arm-source, Undo-restores-link sequence leaves the source armed. Completing a different target replaces the old edge; the next Undo clears the edge rather than restoring the original connection. Directly selecting an already linked source is normally rejected.
Action: Validate the pending source at commit and preserve complete before/after edge state for any permitted replacement.
Acceptance: Remove, arm, restore with Undo, then commit a target: reject the stale action safely or permit one atomic replacement whose Undo restores the exact old link.

Title: Boundary placement can exceed a district's producer limit
Observation: For a 2x2 Phishing footprint crossing adjacent Intel regions, placement checks the origin region while occupancy counts its center region. The fixture admits a producer into a full center region and remaining slots change from 0 to -1.
Action: Choose one authoritative owning district or require a single-district footprint and use it for both validation and accounting.
Acceptance: A boundary build cannot exceed any declared slot limit, and its preview identifies the same owning district used after placement.

Title: Lab and Forge rates are rounded to incorrect whole numbers
Observation: Converter text uses %.0f/s, displaying both Lab's actual 0.5/s and Forge's actual 0.6/s as 1/s. Players plan supply against substantially overstated rates.
Action: Format fractional rates with adequate precision and derive all input/output/fuel values from CONV.
Acceptance: The inspector shows Lab 0.5 Research/s and Forge 0.6 Tools/s with their actual fuel and input requirements.

Title: Proxy inspection still describes the donor's production
Observation: Converted Phishing correctly has a Proxy title but retains the producer homage and 'Sweeps Intel within 6 tiles'. Its production has actually stopped.
Action: Use effective relay identity for description, range, color and operational controls; keep donor provenance separate.
Acceptance: A converted producer's inspector explains forwarding, vision and upkeep and does not claim donor production; reversal restores the donor description.

Title: Quarantine is misdiagnosed as a missing physical path
Observation: A node with a valid parent pointing to C2 and 4.9 seconds of quarantine shows 'OFFLINE - no path to C2'. This suggests rebuilding an intact connection rather than waiting or repairing quarantine.
Action: Report the operational cause and remaining quarantine separately from physical connectivity.
Acceptance: Quarantine on an intact branch displays remaining time and affected nodes; an actually severed branch still reports its missing connection.

Title: Hot-Trace loss is attributed to distance
Observation: A two-cell DNS at hot Trace shows 22% distance loss. The formula has 3% distance loss and a separate 20% ICE multiplier, for 77.6% survival. Shortening the link cannot remove the full reported loss.
Action: Store loss components and display actionable advice for each active cause.
Acceptance: The fixture reports 3% distance and 20% Trace effects with 77.6% combined survival, rather than calling all loss distance.

Title: Sweep remaining-hop count includes the destination node
Observation: A sweep path [node,C2] at step 0 reports 2 hops although only one edge remains. The current count uses node count minus step.
Action: Count remaining transitions, and preferably display an estimated arrival time as well.
Acceptance: One-edge and multi-edge paths report path.size - step - 1 transitions and reach zero at C2.

Title: Crypto laundering shares the saturation it supposedly diversifies away from
Observation: All credits-producing converters use _market_price(), so a Mixer also produces only 0.5 Cash per Crypto at 1000 banked Cash. The code and older design explanation imply diversification avoids Intel saturation; it currently does not.
Action: Choose and document a distinct Mixer exchange policy or remove the unsupported economic claim; evaluate full-chain investment returns.
Acceptance: Mixer payouts at 0, 500 and 1000 Cash match the displayed chosen rule and the documented reason to invest in Crypto.

Title: The described global hot-Trace throttle compounds per hop
Observation: The source applies x0.8 survival to each edge and tests admission at each hop. Ignoring other losses, four hops retain 0.8^4 = 40.96%, whereas the older description calls it a whole-network x0.8 throttle. The formula is analytical source evidence, not a sampled four-hop run.
Action: Choose route-wide or per-edge security loss explicitly and show the end-to-end consequence in route diagnostics.
Acceptance: One-hop and four-hop fixtures match the chosen global or per-hop rule, and backbones are balanced against that actual rule.

Title: Onion advice promises additional reach despite the same route limit
Observation: Every protocol has a 255-cell route limit. A failed route hint recommends Onion for over-length routes, but Onion cannot extend that limit; it only has lower distance loss.
Action: Explain Onion's actual lower-loss niche or implement a deliberately distinct reach rule; separate length failures from geometry failures.
Acceptance: An over-length route succeeds under an explicitly longer Onion limit, or the failure text no longer recommends an equally limited protocol as its remedy.
